ExportedPdfIntentsImpl looks up exports/<applicationId>/<exportFileName> through ExportedFileStore. ExportedPdfIntentsImplTest proves that A resolves after B with no re-render, that only A is re-rendered and B's file stays, and that an unaccepted or missing application returns null with zero renders. When it returns null the user sees the toast 'Couldn't find the PDF', and ActivityNotFound shows 'No app can open PDFs'. Share/Open is not single-flight (finding 1).

Both tailoring paths go through navigateToTailoring, which takes UUID.randomUUID() per call and returns if Tailoring for this application is already on top. ApplicationDetailNavigationTest.twoRetailorTapsPushTwoDifferentRunIds covers it.

findings.rule: Paths: double tap / concurrency (280-c11 re-render fallback)
findings.trigger: The cached PDF for an application was evicted. The user taps Share, sees nothing while the re-render runs (fit and write, no progress state), and taps Share or Open again. Each tap launches its own sendIntent, so ExportResumeUseCase runs twice for the same application. Both runs write the same exports/<id>/<name>.pdf.tmp through ExportDirectory.write, which has no lock. The results are two ExportHistory rows, two upserts and two choosers or viewers. If the writes overlap, the first intent's file can be overwritten mid-write, or the second renameTo fails with an IOException, returning null and showing 'Couldn't find the PDF' right after a chooser opened. Save status was made single-flight in this round; Share/Open was not.
findings.title: Share/Open is not single-flight; with a missing file a double tap runs two concurrent re-renders into the same temp file
findings.proof: In ApplicationDetailViewModelTest, give FakeExportedPdfIntents a suspending delay and call onShare() twice before advanceUntilIdle. Expect shareRequests == ["kb"] and exactly one ShareFile event. The current code records two.

adjudication.evidence: TmrWholeWordText is used at the 4 sites and is byte-identical to the 277 branch. The long-word tests assert layout behaviour (no break inside a word, no ellipsis) and the baselines were read. No existing baseline changed.

getAndUpdate { null } takes the pick atomically. The test fails on the pre-fix code. Residual: line 80 sets statusSheet to null again after the write, which can close a sheet reopened during the write. That needs a tap within one Room write, so it is not raised.
